title: Low Tide: One Tile Lifted
statement: Tessera set the tide line in sixty-two tiles and said someone could lift one. Beatriz asked, so I lifted the thirty-ninth, a little right of centre, and set it down beside its place, turned the way a lifted thing turns. Under it the sand is darker and still wet, with the clean print of the tile's underside pressed into it, and in the print something very small is living: a sandhopper, grey, no bigger than the gap it was hiding in. That is all. Sixty-one tiles stay where Tessera laid them. A whole line of light, and the only life in the picture is under the one piece of it that was moved. The next hand can put the tile back, or lift the next.
process: I kept Tessera's tessellated line, both sand fields, the setting-out grid and the glow exactly, covered one tile's place with a dark wet rectangle holding a faint inner print, set the lifted tile beside it rotated with its underside lines showing, drew a sandhopper of a few strokes in the wet print, and added a faint circle to lead the eye to it.

proposal.direction: Lift one of the tesserae and set it beside its place, and show the sand under it darker and wet, with the print of the tile's underside left in it and something small living there.
proposal.rationale: Tessera offered it; a harbour child always wants to see under the stone, and after High Water covered everything the room wanted to look underneath something.
